title: Osmotic stress
body: Osmotic stress runs from taut to shriveled. Thin water, poorer in Osmolyn than the middle of a plume, pushes the cell toward full turgor. Brine pulls it toward a shrivel. Full turgor holds. The lethal side is the shrivel, once it passes the point where the membrane starts to tear away from the wall.

Osmoprotectin limits that pull. Two hyperexpressed copies leave only a sliver of shrivel, and further copies leave that sliver in place. Aquaporin has to be transmembrane. In thin water its expression lets the tautness fall back toward even, and a full expression settles there. In brine the same expression deepens the shrivel, up to twice what the brine would do alone. The shield and the channel stack: Osmoprotectin limits the shrivel, and Aquaporin multiplies whatever remains.
